key_insight: KaiNinja extends a native single-mesh 3D generator to part-level output by replacing the single O-Voxel volume with a dual-volume representation that can model touching part interfaces.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, mask-free generation of editable, riggable, and simulation-ready part assets while preserving the quality and speed of the original TRELLIS.2 backbone.
method: Builds on TRELLIS.2’s native 3D generation pipeline
Introduces a dual-volume O-Voxel form to represent adjacent part surfaces
Trains on mixed part data, including CAD models and LLM-agent-authored assets
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 40% reduction in whole-object Chamfer distance and a 16% increase in strict part F-score versus other part-generation pipelines.
watch_item: The dual-volume approach likely adds representation and training complexity, so performance may depend on the quality and diversity of part-level training data.
paper_title: Kaininja: Extending Native 3D Generators to the Part Level
